notes.summary: Entity links no longer slow a long chat while an answer streams: finished messages are not read or mounted again per chunk, and markdownComponents keep their identity.
notes.howTo: Use useChatEntityLinks().markdownComponents as JSX, in react-markdown components, or call them inside a function component: they now read React context, and a direct call elsewhere (class render, event handler) throws "Invalid hook call". Otherwise nothing to do. What an app can notice (the CHANGELOG lists every difference): a custom components.MentionChip in a finished message is no longer unmounted and mounted again per chunk; useChatEntityLinks() and its markdownComponents keep their identity; in text parts rendered without Markdown (EntityText) a matcher chip follows a changed hit, new matchers apply to finished messages, and resolveAmbiguous is called less often. Apps that change messages in place (not the AI SDK) should replace a changed output, input or result object rather than mutate it.

notes.summary: While an answer streams, only that message renders and parses its Markdown; a finished message renders only when something it shows changes. No code change needed; keep config objects stable.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do for the speed-up. Check custom components rendered inside a message (components.MessageBubble with useMessageParts, MessageParts, Markdown, MentionChip, ToolResultBlock, tool renderers, ApprovalEntry, ApprovalCard, ClarificationCard, TurnNotice): they no longer render on every chunk of a later answer. A value that was only refreshed by those renders, such as Date.now() or a relative time computed in render, or state read in render without a subscription (a module variable, a ref, localStorage, an external store without useSyncExternalStore), stays as it was until the message renders again; keep it in state, a subscription or a timer. Effects without a dependency list and render logging run less often. A component that calls useChatContext() itself still renders on every change of the chat context. Apps that change message objects in place should replace them instead (the AI SDK does). Keep config stable to get the speed-up: built anew on every render of the component holding the provider, classNames, components, toolLabels, toolResults, entityDeclarations, composer, markdown, toolRenderers, chatInteractions, locale, locales, triggers, entityLinks and approvalDescription render every message per chunk, as before (activityLog, messageFooter, approvalDisplay and suggestions are keyed on their fields). Use a module constant, or useMemo for config that depends on state. After a change pass a new object: a change made in place to classNames, components, toolLabels entries, toolResults.allowlist, entityDeclarations entries, composer, markdown options, toolRenderers entries or chatInteractions entities and passed as the same object shows in a finished message only once it renders again. The CHANGELOG lists every difference.
